candidates.lead: Domestic abuse charity Endeavour welcomed the national rollout but said more work was needed
candidates.evidence_text: Domestic abuse prevention orders a 'step in right direction' - BBC News Image caption, Jill Caldwell, who is chief executive of domestic abuse charity Endeavour, welcomed the new orders By Mairead Smyth , North West and Lauren Hirst , North West Published 1 hour ago A charity has welcomed the rollout of domestic abuse protection orders (DAPOs) across England and Wales but warned more needs to be done to protect and support victims. Under new restrictions, abusers could be forced to hand over house keys, social media passwords, phones and laptops in a bid to protect victims. Jill Caldwell, chief executive of Bolton-based domestic abuse charity Endeavour, said the rollout was "a really good start" but the government needed to ensure the orders were effectively enforced by police and specialist support services were in place for victims. Home Secretary, Shabana Mahmood, said the government was " rolling out the strongest protections ever available to victims". , external "This government is taking action and will always stand with victims and survivors of domestic abuse," she said. A DAPO can be made by a court to protect victims from all forms of domestic abuse, including non-physical abuse and controlling or coercive behaviour. Applications can also be made by the police, the victim or someone who is not directly involved, known as a third party - such as family member, a friend, or a social worker. Those who breach the order could be charged with a criminal offence, punishable by up to five years in prison. Unlike previous protections, DAPOs can remain in place for as long as necessary in a bid to keep victims safe. Image source, Press Association Image caption, DAPOs can be used to impose restrictions and conditions on a perpetrator of domestic abuse "The positive thing with DAPOs from my point of view is that it puts the onus more on the person causing the harm than the victim and that is a really positive step," said Caldwell. "It prohibits the offender, so it might be in terms of where they can go and how much contact they can have with the victim. "But it also puts positive reinforcements in there as well, so it could be that they are asked to attend a behaviour change programme. "And it's really refreshing to see something where actually the onus is on the person causing the harm and on the victim trying to keep themselves safe." But she said the effectiveness of DAPOs was reliant on enforcement. "The DAPO is only as good as the enforcement so if it's been breached you need to know that it's been properly enforced and that the proper measures are in place as well," she said. "I think there are several different ways to go yet but it's a really good start. "It was a positive thing from the Domestic Abuse Act that came in but, as with all things, it's making sure legal protections are in place, making sure enforcement is there, but also making sure specialist support services are in place. "You need all three to actually move towards the government's intention of halving violence against women and girls." 'More robust' Greater Manchester was one of five areas who trialled the use of the DAPOs across the country. Since the pilot began in November 2024, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said it had issued 1,825 orders across all 10 boroughs. The force said it had robustly dealt with more than 700 breaches, most of which will have received jail time, a suspended sentence, fine or community order. Det Supt Jen Tattersall from GMP, from GMP, said: "We have done a really successful DAPO pilot. "As a result of that, I think that reported and recorded domestic abuse crime has come down because we are more robust with our perpetrators". candidates.lead: Police are investigating a possible link between the Co-op Live evacuation and reported robberies
candidates.evidence_text: Substance at Don Toliver Manchester show may be linked to robberies, police say - BBC News Image source, Getty Images Image caption, The substance was released near the end of US rapper Don Toliver's gig at Co-op Live on Sunday By Richard Baker North West Published 24 November 2026 An "unknown substance" that prompted a mass evacuation at a rap concert may be linked to robberies and stolen jewellery at the venue, police have said. More than 12,000 people were evacuated from Manchester's Co-op Live during a performance by US rapper Don Toliver on Sunday. One person was taken to hospital and 88 others were treated at the scene after concertgoers reported a "horrible smell" and some people "coughing up blood". Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said officers received nine reports of jewellery being stolen during the concert but no arrests had been made and the substance had not yet been identified. Image source, PA MEDIA Image caption, The police scene has now been lifted at Co-op Live Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said there was "no wider ongoing risk" to the public. "We are aware similar robberies have been reported at two European concerts for the same artist and will be linking in with our European counterparts to better understand the wider picture of this suspected offending," he said. In a statement on Tuesday evening, Co-op Live said it was conducting a "full review" into the incident. "The safety and security of our guests, artists and staff remain our highest priority, and we take that responsibility extremely seriously." The venue, which opened in 2024, apologised to fans for what should have been an "enjoyable evening" and said it expects no disruption to future events. The substance was released at around 22:00 GMT, near the end of Toliver's show as part of his Nitrous – Octane world tour. Afterwards, 88 people underwent dry decontamination at the scene and were accommodated at the neighbouring Etihad Stadium while the incident was managed. Many were advised to seal their clothes in a bag overnight. Image source, HANDOUT Image caption, Friends Poppy Rutter and Sophie Billing say they felt "unsafe" as they left the arena Poppy Rutter and Sophie Billing, both 19, who had travelled from Cambridge to see the concert, said it was not immediately clear what had happened. Sophie said: "I thought something had gone wrong with smoke coming off stage. "We started to suffer, coughing and spluttering and feeling tight-chested. A member of staff said it was tear gas. "Security rushed in and went straight to the pit. We only left as we were starting to feel unsafe and not 100 per cent well." She said there was "no communication", adding: "You would think Manchester would be extra vigilant, given what's happened in the past." Posting on Instagram on Monday, Toliver said: "I just wanna make sure everyone is safe and the next show goes on properly. My heart and prayers are with everyone that was injured last night at Co-op Live. "The only thing I love more than creating music is performing for my fans." He also asked that people stop bringing substances into his shows. GMP urged anyone who feels unwell or develops symptoms following the concert to seek medical advice. candidates.lead: The former Manchester City defender denies failing to provide driver information to police
candidates.evidence_text: John Stones faces 2028 trial over alleged motoring offence - BBC News Image source, Press Association Image caption, The former Manchester City defender has pleaded not guilty Published 18 minutes ago England defender John Stones faces trial in 2028 over an allegation he failed to provide driver information to police. The 32-year-old footballer, who left Manchester City for Inter Milan this summer , is alleged to have driven his £150,000 Range Rover at 58mph (93km/h) in a 50mph zone on the M60 in March 2026. Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said Stones did not respond to two letters and on 27 April was charged with failing to furnish driver information. He has since pleaded not guilty. Stones is represented by Freeman & Co Solicitors, a law firm whose owner Nick Freeman has advised several celebrity clients in motoring cases and has trademarked his nickname of Mr Loophole. Stones now faces trial on 29 September 2028 at Warrington Magistrates' Court. He has denied receiving the request for information from the police and asked prosecutors to prove it was served. In a letter to the court, Stones's lawyers added: "It was not reasonably practicable for the defendant to give the information within the requisite period." They also claimed GMP included "hearsay" in its single justice procedure notice dated 20 October 2026. Stones's team requested that the trial should last at least two hours and be heard in the morning. They also asked for permission for him to be excused from a pre-trial case management hearing were one to be required. Image source, Press Association Image caption, The England defender joined Inter Milan in the summer after 10 years at Manchester City Earlier this year Stones was convicted of speeding and landed with a £1,052 court bill after he missed a police letter while at the World Cup in the United States and Mexico with England. He had been caught driving his Range Rover at 43mph along a country lane near his Cheshire mansion in May. Stones admitted being the driver when first contacted by Cheshire Police, but did not respond to a second letter offering him the chance to pay a fixed penalty to keep the speeding offence out of court. He was then prosecuted and convicted in the single justice procedure, with a magistrate last week issuing him four penalty points and ordering him to pay a £666 fine, £120 in costs and a £266 victim surcharge. Stones wrote to Warrington Magistrates' Court to say: "Nothing to say about the speeding. "The reason I am only responding to the offence now is because I represent our country for football and so I have not been home and seen any post. "I sent off my letter on the 28th May to give my details [and then] I went off to join England. "We were there until the 19th July. "I went on holiday and then moved to Milan, so this has been found by chance, as no-one has been home for almost four months. "This is the reason I also would not be able to be present as I no longer am residing in the country." Central defender Stones, who played for Barnsley and Everton before a 10-year spell with Manchester City, has made four appearances so far for Inter Milan since his summer switch to the San Siro. candidates.evidence_text: Restaurant boss banned over £363k furlough claims - BBC News Image source, Google Maps Image caption, The Laundrette opened on Beech Road in Chorlton in 2013 By Haider Saleem North West Published 24 November 2026 The co-founder of a restaurant has been banned from acting as a company director for five years after his company failed to account for over £363,000 in furlough payments during the coronavirus pandemic, the Insolvency Service said. Patrick Hall, 45, helped establish The Laundrette in Chorlton, Manchester, which closed in 2025 after 12 years in business, citing "rising costs and insufficient government support". The Insolvency Service said Winchester Services Limited, which ran the restaurant, repeatedly failed to provide evidence that it was entitled to the payments. Hall, from Levenshulme, agreed to a disqualification undertaking and a five-year ban. The restaurant and bar, known for its pizzas and cocktails, opened on Beech Road in 2013 and was run through several companies under Hall's directorship. Winchester Services Limited received the furlough payments between April 2020 and May 2021. HMRC began examining the claims in July 2022, but the company failed to provide the required information despite being given additional time. In January 2023, HMRC demanded repayment of the full amount and imposed penalties of £344,888 on the company for what it said was a deliberate failure to report the overpayments. When the company went into liquidation in March 2023, it had liabilities of more than £913,000, including nearly £708,000 owed to HMRC over the furlough claims and penalties. 'Government support' Kevin Read, chief investigator at the Insolvency Service, said: "Despite repeated requests and additional time to provide evidence, the company failed to demonstrate that its claims were valid. "The furlough scheme provided vital support to businesses during the pandemic, but that support was not unconditional." The restaurant continued trading under another company, of which Hall was also a director, until its closure in 2025. Announcing its planned closure on 29 September 2025, The Laundrette blamed "rising costs and insufficient government support". In its closure announcement, the restaurant said it had been ranked first in Manchester on TripAdvisor for more than five years. In a statement on X in September 2025, it thanked customers and staff and described the restaurant as a "community hub filled with laughter, friendships, and countless celebrations". The ban prevents him from setting up or managing a company, directly or indirectly, without permission from a court. HMRC declined to comment on whether any of the furlough payments had been recovered, citing confidentiality. candidates.evidence_text: Memorial plaques and urns worth £20k stolen from Stockport cemetery - BBC News Image caption, Police said the theft took place between 17:30 on Sunday and 05:30 on Monday By Georgie Docker and Richard Stead , North West Published 24 November 2026 Memorial plaques and grave ornaments worth more than £20,000 have been stolen from a cemetery in Stockport. A volunteer at St Mark's Church in Bredbury discovered about 94 cast-iron memorial plaques and 80 stone and granite flower urns had been stolen at about 05:30 GMT on Monday. Greater Manchester Police said the total estimated value of the stolen items is in excess of £20,000, adding "this figure may increase as further families visit the churchyard and report additional missing items". "You just can't believe it," Reverend Andy Bull said. "For the plaques to have disappeared - the sentimental value of that is huge to people." Image caption, Reverend Andy Bull said it was 'hard to comprehend' that someone would steal memorial plaques and urns Police estimated the memorial plaques were worth more than £8,000 and the stone and granite urns more than £12,000. But Bull said the loss to families was far greater. "People have a very strong affiliation with the graveyard. It's a place where they come to remember loved ones," he said. "A lot of people are feeling very sad that a place which was there to remember loved ones has become fraught with emotions." GMP said it was reviewing CCTV footage to identify any people or vehicles in the area during the period of the theft. candidates.lead: Greater Manchester's School Streets scheme encourages more children to walk, cycle or scoot to school
candidates.evidence_text: Banning cars near schools at rush hour 'would make big difference' - BBC News Image caption, The Dean Trust academy in Ardwick is one of the schools wanting to join the School Streets scheme By Davinia Ramos North West Published 24 November 2026 A head teacher has said he would support his school joining a scheme designed to ban most cars from parking around it during peak times. Steven Worthington, who runs the Dean Trust Ardwick in east Manchester, said there had been "a number of incidents" and "our young people are subjected to bad traffic pollution". He told the BBC that "traffic is very congested during school drop-off and pick-up times... we're keen to address this''. Greater Manchester's School Streets initiative - which also encourages children to walk, cycle or scoot - was launched five years ago and now covers 51 schools and more than 20,000 pupils. By 2030, Transport for Greater Manchester wants 70% of primary school pupils to walk, wheel, scoot or cycle to and from school. Image caption, The School Streets programme is designed to persuade more children to walk to and from school Roads surrounding the Dean Trust Academy are chaotic at peak times, with motorists often parking on double yellow lines or leaving their engines running while waiting for their children to finish school. One parent Lisa Moores said: "It's really busy - loads of children are trying to cross the road at the same time and cars are trying to navigate round them, I've had a few run-ins with people not giving way. "Having restrictions down here would make a big difference during certain times of day." Worthington said he would like to implement the School Streets programme. Under it, traffic is restricted at drop-off and pick-up times on certain roads surrounding schools. Anyone who breaches the restrictions and is filmed by ANPR cameras gets a written warning. Repeat offenders are fined £70. 'Giving parents a choice' One of the schools that has signed up to the scheme is Acacias Community Primary School in Burnage, south Manchester. During two periods - from 08:15 to 09:00 and 15:00 to 15:45 - vehicle access around the school is restricted on weekdays. Roads are only open to pedestrians, cyclists, and exempted vehicles such as emergency services, Blue Badge holders and eligible local residents. Greater Manchester's active travel commissioner Dame Sarah Storey said: "This is about giving parents a choice, lots of people don't feel it's safe for their children to walk to school and this scheme encourages them to do so". One parent of a pupil at Acacias said: "I think it's a great idea to walk to school and safer not to drive. "There are too many cars on the road, and this is much better and healthier." candidates.lead: Jamie, 17, has had two emergency operations since falling from a sixth-floor balcony on 10 November
candidates.evidence_text: Benidorm balcony fall: Bury teen Jamie opens eyes after two weeks - BBC News Image source, Family handout Image caption, Jamie, 17, has shown signs of improvement but remains seriously ill in hospital By Haider Saleem North West Published 24 November 2026 A teenager who fell from a sixth-floor hotel balcony in Spain has opened his eyes and responded to his relatives after spending nearly two weeks in intensive care, his family has said. Jamie, 17, was seriously injured in Benidorm on 10 November and has had two emergency operations. His family, from Bury in Greater Manchester, said doctors had been reducing Jamie's sedation and went on to say that he had responded to their voices and had followed instructions. While the teenager's lungs are improving, he remains seriously ill, still requires support from a ventilator and faces further surgery, they said. Image source, Family handout Image caption, Jamie remains seriously ill in hospital in Alicante, Spain, where he has undergone two emergency operations "After so many days of seeing him heavily sedated, we finally got to see those eyes open, see him looking at us, responding to our voices and following instructions," the family said. "After nearly two weeks of worry, waiting and uncertainty, those moments meant more to us than we could ever put into words." Jamie had been on holiday with his mum Gemma and her friends. His aunt Lauren said the family did not know the circumstances which led to him falling from the balcony. Describing how she felt when she learned what had happened, Lauren said it had been "the worst phone call of my life". She described her close relationship with keen football fan Jamie and said they had spent time together at matches. Image source, Family handout Image caption, Jamie's aunt Lauren has set up a fundraising appeal to help bring him home Following the fall, Jamie was initially treated in Benidorm before being transferred to a hospital in Alicante. According to his family, surgeons inserted a stent to repair a ruptured artery and used an external metal frame to stabilise his severely fractured pelvis. He also suffered broken legs and an arm, fractures to his chest and a punctured lung, according to a fundraising appeal set up by Lauren. Further surgery on his pelvis had been postponed because of a lung infection. Image source, Family handout Image caption, Jamie is a keen football fan who attends matches with his aunt Lauren has launched a £20,000 fundraising appeal to help cover costs not met by their insurance or charities, including bringing Jamie back to the UK and expenses for his family while he remains in hospital. In their latest update, the family thanked people for their donations and messages of support. The BBC has asked both the hotel and Spanish police about the incident. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A teenager who fell from a sixth-floor hotel balcony in Spain has opened his eyes and responded to his relatives after spending nearly two weeks in intensive care, his family has said Jamie, 17, was seriously injured in Benidorm on 10 November and has had two emergency operations His family, from Bury in Greater Manchester, said doctors had been reducing Jamie's sedation and went on to say that he had responded to their voices and had followed instructions While the teenager's lungs are improving, he remains seriously ill, still requires support from a ventilator and faces further surgery, they said "After so many days of seeing him heavily sedated, we finally got to see those eyes open, see him looking at us, responding to our voices and following instructions," the family said "After nearly two weeks of worry, waiting and uncertainty, those moments meant more to us than we could ever put into words."

"The lads who I was with basically said the colour drained out of me immediately." Third-party provider Swissport, which carries out Ryanair's checks at Manchester Airport where Moore flew from, said it was now reinforcing mandatory boarding procedures Moore, who was travelling to Alicante on a stag party with friends, told BBC Radio Stoke he initially thought he must have picked up his wife's passport in addition to his own He said he approached Spanish police who - along with the language barrier - appeared to be as confused as he was about how he had turned up there without his own passport

candidates.evidence_text: Russell Brand Andy Burnham calls for 'watershed moment' as government makes move after Russell Brand rape conviction 'Too often, the powerful have been protected and the vulnerable exploited' Add to preferred sources Comments News PA and Paul Britton Prime Minister Andy Burnham has called for a “watershed moment” following Russell Brand’s rape conviction as the Government moves to make it harder to silence victims through non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) Writing in The Guardian, Mr Burnham argued that powerful men should no longer be able to use their fame and wealth to get away with abuse. "Too often, the powerful have been protected and the vulnerable exploited,” he said “We need to get to a place where women and girls feel confident that if they report a crime, they will be treated with dignity and compassion and action will be taken." On Tuesday, the Government said plans to curb the use of NDAs would be brought forward to January The changes under the Employment Rights Act and the Victims and Courts Act will void clauses in NDAs if they are used to silence workers over harassment or discrimination or to stop victims reporting information about criminal conduct

candidates.evidence_text: Courts A couple in court and their phone that received 1,861 calls in two weeks Carl Lomas was arrested and then bailed, on the condition that he did not return to the area where he had been arrested - but he did it anyway Both defendants were homeles Add to preferred sources Comments News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 05:55, 25 Nov 2026 Updated 06:10, 25 Nov 2026 A drug dealer who 'simply continued to peddle heroin and crack cocaine' following his arrest has found himself hauled before the courts alongside his girlfriend Carl Lomas and Sarah Warburton were both found with heroin and crack cocaine after officers swooped in Stockport . A ‘burner’ phone used to supply drugs received 1,861 incoming calls within a two week period before it was seized in July The pair, who were both remanded in prison, were sentenced at Minshull Street Crown Court in Manchester yesterday (November 24). Lomas was jailed while Warburton was handed a suspended prison sentence Prosecuting, Andy Evans said that an officer was on patrol in Heaton Norris on November 19 last year when Lomas emerged from a house said to have been linked to drug dealing The officer stopped Lomas, who was found to be in possession of 11.1g of heroin and 6.88g of crack cocaine. He also had a Nokia ‘burner’ phone and £213 in cash. He was arrested and then bailed, on the condition that he did not return to the area where he had been arrested

Jamie, 17, was on holiday with his mum, Gemma, 36, and her friends for Fiesta Week when he fell from the sixth floor his hotel, the s The teen underwent two emergency operations in Alicante and was heavily sedated after he suffered extensive injuries. Jamie fractured both sides of his chest, punctured a lung, ruptured an artery, and broke bones in his pelvis, both legs and one arm on November 10 His family said Jamie opened his eyes on Sunday (November 22) and followed instructions after doctors reduced his sedation. Despite his progress, Jamie remains seriously ill and continues to require support from a ventilator, The Mirror reports His family said: "Over the last few days, Jamie has started showing some encouraging signs of improvement. His lungs are looking better, the amount of oxygen he's needing has reduced, and the doctors have been gradually trying to bring him out of sedation "After so many days of seeing him heavily sedated, we finally got to see those eyes open, see him looking at us, responding to our voices and following instructions. candidates.evidence_text: Rochdale 'Truth has its own power': The Rochdale veteran whose decades-long fight for justice may soon be over John Morris was one of thousands of young men posted to Christmas Island as part of Operation Grapple, Britain’s campaign to build and test A nuclear test veteran from Rochdale who has spent decades fighting for answers following the death of his baby son says he hopes he will live long enough to see justice finally delivered John Morris, 89, has welcomed the announcement of an independent panel into the impact of Britain's nuclear weapons testing, describing it as a breakthrough after what he believes has been a cover-up of several decades The panel, announced by Prime Minister Andy Burnham , will be chaired by Bishop James Jones and investigate the potential impact of nuclear testing on veterans and their families It will follow the model of the Hillsborough Independent Panel, also chaired by Bishop Jones, with the aim of delivering an interim report in time for the 75th anniversary of Britain's first nuclear weapons test For John, who witnessed four nuclear explosions in 1957, the announcement represents a significant moment in a campaign that has spanned much of his life

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale 'Truth has its own power': The Rochdale veteran whose decades-long fight for justice may soon be over John Morris was one of thousands of young men posted to Christmas Island as part of Operation Grapple, Britain’s campaign to build and test A nuclear test veteran from Rochdale who has spent decades fighting for answers following the death of his baby son says he hopes he will live long enough to see justice finally delivered John Morris, 89, has welcomed the announcement of an independent panel into the impact of Britain's nuclear weapons testing, describing it as a breakthrough after what he believes has been a cover-up of several decades The panel, announced by Prime Minister Andy Burnham , will be chaired by Bishop James Jones and investigate the potential impact of nuclear testing on veterans and their families It will follow the model of the Hillsborough Independent Panel, also chaired by Bishop Jones, with the aim of delivering an interim report in time for the 75th anniversary of Britain's first nuclear weapons test For John, who witnessed four nuclear explosions in 1957, the announcement represents a significant moment in a campaign that has spanned much of his life

candidates.evidence_text: Stockport Outrage as Stockport graveyard decimated by callous thieves who make off with £20k of urns and plaques Police are appealing for information Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 18:14, 24 Nov 2026 Cast iron pla A Stockport church has been left devastated after almost 200 memorial urns and plaques were stolen from its graveyard. Nearly 100 cast iron memorial plaques and 80 granite and stone flower urns were removed from the graveyard of St Mark's Church on Redhouse Lane in Bredbury this The missing and damaged plaques were discovered by a volunteer at the church at around 5.30am on Sunday morning (November 23). Photos from the churchyard show dozens of missing plaques from a memorial area of the church yard, with some remaining plaques chipped and broken The Stockport branch of Greater Manchester Police is now appealing for information following the theft, as they estimate the total value of the stolen property to be more than £20,000, alongside its 'substantial' sentimental value The force said that 94 memorial plaques and 80 memorial urns had been removed and stolen from graves throughout the church yard, with an estimated value of £8k and £12k respectively Memorial plaques were stolen from the graveyard (Image: Sean Hansford | Manchester Evening News)

english_fact_card.what_happened: An initial consultation on the long-planned Wigan to Hindley link road (WHLR) ends this week, with hopes that building will begin in 2029. The 2.5km single carriageway road would take traffic from the A49 Westwood Way to the A5777 Manchester Road, including links with Warrington Road, Phoenix Way, Seaman Way and south to Liverpool Road. The project has been an aspiration since 1949 and is part of an east-west route eventually linking the M6 and M61.
english_fact_card.when: Consultation ends this week (week of 24 November 2026); construction hoped to begin in 2029.
english_fact_card.who_affected: Residents and road users in Wigan and Hindley; the wider area if the route eventually links the M6 and M61.
english_fact_card.why_now: The consultation is closing, and the government committed £153m to the scheme in March 2026.

candidates.evidence_text: Co-Op Live 'Tests ongoing' to identify substance that sparked Don Toliver Co-op Live concert evacuation Manchester council leader Garry Bridges said it remained a 'devleoping incident' Add to preferred sources News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 14:05, 24 N Tests are ongoing to identify an unknown substance that sparked the evacuation of Co-op Live during a gig by US rapper Don Toliver , Manchester council's leader has said. More than 12,000 people were inside the venue as a major incident was declared on Sunday night One person was taken to hospital and 89 concert-goers were treated at the scene . Police initially said tear gas was thought to have been released inside the arena , but later described it as an 'unknown substance' Mobile phone video footage showed concert-goers struggling to breathe and coughing as they walked out of the venue. In a statement today, Manchester council leader Garry Bridges said it remained a 'developing incident' He told Sky News: "Tests are still ongoing to determine the nature of the substance that was released. This is a developing incident and we, alongside our partners, are working to establish the facts of what took place on Sunday evening." Coun Bridges also thanked emergency services, and urged any concert-goer who experiences adverse symptoms to contact their GP, ring 111 or go to hospital

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Historic £1.4m Salford church with 4am party licence up for sale - and the extraordinary story of the street around it Built in 1819 in a post-Napoleonic surge of religious fervour - and later rocked by a minister's mysterious scandal - the Gr Add to preferred sources Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 06:23, 24 Nov 2026 An empty Georgian church may be on the brink of salvation. The former Hope United Reformed Church in Chapel Street, Salford , dates from 1819 Close to Manchester city centre and less than 100 yards from Salford Central railway station it ceased to be a regular place of worship several years ago. Grade II listed, it is now up for sale for offers in excess of £1.4m Its roots lie in a surge of "Christian fervour" across the country at the end of the Napoleonic Wars. It sprang from a dearth of places to hear the Gospel in the rapidly industrialising Salford. It survived as a church through name changes, and the resignation of its first leader A dwindling congregation eventually meant a final Sunday Service was held in 2019. In 2023 plans to convert it into a complex of flats, a community centre and commercial use were submitted to the City Council Hope United Reformed Church on Chapel St, Salford, pictured today. It is up for sale for £1.4m. (Image: Manchester Evening News)

candidates.evidence_text: Courts A couple in court and their phone that received 1,861 calls in two weeks Carl Lomas was arrested and then bailed, on the condition that he did not return to the area where he had been arrested - but he did it anyway Both defendants were homeles Add to preferred sources Comments News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 05:55, 25 Nov 2026 Updated 06:10, 25 Nov 2026 A drug dealer who 'simply continued to peddle heroin and crack cocaine' following his arrest has found himself hauled before the courts alongside his girlfriend Carl Lomas and Sarah Warburton were both found with heroin and crack cocaine after officers swooped in Stockport . A ‘burner’ phone used to supply drugs received 1,861 incoming calls within a two week period before it was seized in July The pair, who were both remanded in prison, were sentenced at Minshull Street Crown Court in Manchester yesterday (November 24). Lomas was jailed while Warburton was handed a suspended prison sentence Prosecuting, Andy Evans said that an officer was on patrol in Heaton Norris on November 19 last year when Lomas emerged from a house said to have been linked to drug dealing The officer stopped Lomas, who was found to be in possession of 11.1g of heroin and 6.88g of crack cocaine. He also had a Nokia ‘burner’ phone and £213 in cash. He was arrested and then bailed, on the condition that he did not return to the area where he had been arrested

Jamie fractured both sides of his chest, punctured a lung, ruptured an artery, and broke bones in his pelvis, both legs and one arm on November 10 His family said Jamie opened his eyes on Sunday (November 22) and followed instructions after doctors reduced his sedation. Despite his progress, Jamie remains seriously ill and continues to require support from a ventilator, The Mirror reports His family said: "Over the last few days, Jamie has started showing some encouraging signs of improvement. His lungs are looking better, the amount of oxygen he's needing has reduced, and the doctors have been gradually trying to bring him out of sedation "After so many days of seeing him heavily sedated, we finally got to see those eyes open, see him looking at us, responding to our voices and following instructions. candidates.evidence_text: Rochdale 'Truth has its own power': The Rochdale veteran whose decades-long fight for justice may soon be over John Morris was one of thousands of young men posted to Christmas Island as part of Operation Grapple, Britain’s campaign to build and test A nuclear test veteran from Rochdale who has spent decades fighting for answers following the death of his baby son says he hopes he will live long enough to see justice finally delivered John Morris, 89, has welcomed the announcement of an independent panel into the impact of Britain's nuclear weapons testing, describing it as a breakthrough after what he believes has been a cover-up of several decades The panel, announced by Prime Minister Andy Burnham , will be chaired by Bishop James Jones and investigate the potential impact of nuclear testing on veterans and their families It will follow the model of the Hillsborough Independent Panel, also chaired by Bishop Jones, with the aim of delivering an interim report in time for the 75th anniversary of Britain's first nuclear weapons test For John, who witnessed four nuclear explosions in 1957, the announcement represents a significant moment in a campaign that has spanned much of his life

candidates.evidence_text: Stockport Outrage as Stockport graveyard decimated by callous thieves who make off with £20k of urns and plaques Police are appealing for information Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 18:14, 24 Nov 2026 Cast iron pla A Stockport church has been left devastated after almost 200 memorial urns and plaques were stolen from its graveyard. Nearly 100 cast iron memorial plaques and 80 granite and stone flower urns were removed from the graveyard of St Mark's Church on Redhouse Lane in Bredbury this The missing and damaged plaques were discovered by a volunteer at the church at around 5.30am on Sunday morning (November 23). Photos from the churchyard show dozens of missing plaques from a memorial area of the church yard, with some remaining plaques chipped and broken The Stockport branch of Greater Manchester Police is now appealing for information following the theft, as they estimate the total value of the stolen property to be more than £20,000, alongside its 'substantial' sentimental value The force said that 94 memorial plaques and 80 memorial urns had been removed and stolen from graves throughout the church yard, with an estimated value of £8k and £12k respectively Memorial plaques were stolen from the graveyard (Image: Sean Hansford | Manchester Evening News)

More than 12,000 people were inside the venue as a major incident was declared on Sunday night One person was taken to hospital and 89 concert-goers were treated at the scene . Police initially said tear gas was thought to have been released inside the arena , but later described it as an 'unknown substance' Mobile phone video footage showed concert-goers struggling to breathe and coughing as they walked out of the venue. Coun Bridges also thanked emergency services, and urged any concert-goer who experiences adverse symptoms to contact their GP, ring 111 or go to hospital

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Historic £1.4m Salford church with 4am party licence up for sale - and the extraordinary story of the street around it Built in 1819 in a post-Napoleonic surge of religious fervour - and later rocked by a minister's mysterious scandal - the Gr Add to preferred sources Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 06:23, 24 Nov 2026 An empty Georgian church may be on the brink of salvation. The former Hope United Reformed Church in Chapel Street, Salford , dates from 1819 Close to Manchester city centre and less than 100 yards from Salford Central railway station it ceased to be a regular place of worship several years ago. Grade II listed, it is now up for sale for offers in excess of £1.4m Its roots lie in a surge of "Christian fervour" across the country at the end of the Napoleonic Wars. It sprang from a dearth of places to hear the Gospel in the rapidly industrialising Salford. It survived as a church through name changes, and the resignation of its first leader A dwindling congregation eventually meant a final Sunday Service was held in 2019. In 2023 plans to convert it into a complex of flats, a community centre and commercial use were submitted to the City Council Hope United Reformed Church on Chapel St, Salford, pictured today. It is up for sale for £1.4m. (Image: Manchester Evening News)

Head of the racket Christa Cleary wept as she was locked up for six years, whilst Simon McQuillan, who operated one of two drugs lines, hugged his wife before being sent down Manchester Crown Court heard the group supplied and sold the class A and B drugs from August 2024 to October 2025. Described as an 'organised operation', it involved two separate drug phone lines, advertising messages, customer lists and debt record At least one kilo of cocaine and six kilos of cannabis was supplied, the court heard Sentencing, the Recorder of Manchester, Judge Nicholas Dean KC said: "The supply of cocaine causes grave harm. Those selling it sustain addiction, damage health of others and contribute to a lot of the criminality associated with the drugs trade. All of your knew that. Some of yo The court heard that Cleary, 37, was the head of the operation, and was in charge of the supply of drugs. Judge Dean KC said she 'exercised authority and instructed others'

candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 14 October 2026 at 10:33am Kirith Entwistle, the Labour MP for Bolton North East, has said she found the current court system "triggering" and had to watch her abuser "stare at her". Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Monday 12 October 2026 at 5:22pm Credit: Family photo A police officer called to the home of a mother and her four children murdered hours later in an arson attack told a court she thought their killer was making "empty threats" and did not try to arrest him Pc Gemma Quinn told Bolton Coroner's Court she did not think it necessary to arrest Zak Bolland, 26, "there and then" after a 999 call from Michelle Pearson , 37, when he threatened her son and home on Jackson Street in Walkden , Salford Greater Manchester Police's (GMP) Pc Quinn said she planned to arrest Bolland when she was next on shift in two days' time But after she and a more junior colleague left Ms Pearson's home, Bolland returned less than three hours later to murder her and four of her children in a firebomb attack in the early hours of December 11 2017 The firebombing killed four of Michelle's children, Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three Zak Bolland, 26, and David Worrall, 28, were both jailed for life the following year for the murders

Credit: 499883 A man who murdered a mother and four of her children in a firebomb attack had been arrested and released by police despite Zak Bolland, 26, walked free from a police station after giving a 12-minute ‘no comment’ interview for breaking the windows of the home of Michelle Pearson, 37, and her young family in Jackson Street in Walkden, Greater Manchester on November 26 2017 Bolland’s previous convictions and suspended jail sentence he was serving at the time had not been checked by police and he was told he would be ‘NFA’d’ – no further action taken against him over the windows attack, Bolton Coroner’s Court heard Thirteen days later, in the dead of night on December 11 2017, he smashed Ms Pearson’s windows again and tossed in a petrol bomb which “exploded” near the stairs, blocking the only exit to the ground floor and trapping the victims upstairs Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, all died in the blaze Ms Pearson suffered 68% burns to her body and “clung on to life” until she died, 20 months after the attack on August 25 2019

The capital’s go back to 1863 but the first here was installed on a Quay Street building in 1960 for the Free Trade pioneer Richard Cobden. candidates.evidence_text: The proposed parking changes are expected to take effect in summer 2027 Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Trafford councillors have rejected calls to scrap planned parking charges in Timperley and the proposed introduction of evening and Sunday charges across the borough At Wednesday night’s Full Council meeting, a Conservative amendment calling for the proposals to be withdrawn was defeated, while a Labour amendment removing opposition to the extension of parking charges was passed The original Liberal Democrat motion, tabled by Timperley North councillor Jane Brophy, had warned that extending charges to smaller district centres risked damaging businesses already facing significant pressures Labour’s successful amendment removed that commitment, replacing it with a statement that “Parking charges should reflect the different needs and offers in areas across Trafford.” The vote does not, however, mean the proposed charges have been formally approved

candidates.evidence_text: on WhatsApp Share via Email The Government is to end its use of Altrincham's Cresta Court Hotel as accommodation for asylum seekers, more than two years after its sudden closure to the public sparked widespread controversy Altrincham and Sale West MP Connor Rand confirmed today that the remaining asylum seekers will leave the Church Street hotel "over the next few months" The decision follows the closure of the Britannia Ashley Hotel in Hale as asylum accommodation in August and paves the way for the potential return of one of Altrincham's best-known hotels to its former use The announcement marks the beginning of the end of one of the most contentious issues in Altrincham in recent years and raises the prospect of one of the town's best-known hotels returning to commercial use It was on October 29th 2024 that Altrincham Today confirmed that the Cresta Court had been closed to house asylum seekers , having broken the news of its sudden closure the previous evening The 148-bedroom hotel, a fixture of Altrincham's hospitality scene since the 1970s, had shut with immediate effect, leaving customers with existing bookings for weddings, Christmas parties and other events facing last-minute cancellations

candidates.evidence_text: A man who drugged and raped his wife for more than 20 years advertised online "looking for some extra fun and games", a court heard The victim's husband pleaded guilty earlier this year to multiple offences dating from 2004, including rape, sexual assault and administering a substance with intent to commit a sexual offence The man in his 60s, who cannot be identified to protect his wife's anonymity, took images and videos of his offending as she lay "out of it" on their bed, and then shared them online From 2023 onwards at the latest, the prosecution says he began inviting other men to their home in Stockport, Greater Manchester, where it is said they too sexually abused her He will give evidence later this week against nine men on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court over their alleged roles in the offending Several of the defendants initially met the husband through Fabswingers.com, a website for those interested in swinging, before they moved contact to different messaging apps

candidates.evidence_text: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund The funding forms part of an £18million government programme to create or refurbish playgrounds in England's areas of greatest need over the next two years The government selected Failsworth to receive a share of the fund, with three play areas identified as eligible for investment through the programme for 66 local authorities Funding will be used to improve playground facilities and support community-led design and engagement activities, giving residents the opportunity to help shape the future of these spaces The three eligible sites are Higher Memorial Park which will receive £160,000, Daisy Nook Country Park which will receive £60,000 and Lower Memorial Park which has been allocated £50,000 A larger share will go to Higher Memorial Park because this has received significantly less external investment than the other locations in recent years

candidates.evidence_text: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026 The referendum will ask residents whether they want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan to help decide planning applications in the area The plan sets out local planning policies for Saddleworth and, if approved, will become part of the area’s statutory Development Plan, helping to guide decisions on future planning applications Residents will be asked the following question “Do you want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Neighbourhood Plan for Saddleworth to help it decide planning applications in the neighbourhood area?” To vote, residents must be registered to vote in local government elections and have a qualifying address within the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Area

candidates.board_rank_why: Referendum on Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan gives residents a direct say in local planning, though the date is still weeks away.
candidates.digest_selection_reason: Selected in city_watch shortlist before writing.
candidates.english_reader_card: Saddleworth residents will vote on 10 December on whether to adopt the Neighbourhood Plan, which would guide future planning decisions in the area.

english_fact_card.what_happened: A referendum will be held on 10 December 2026 asking Saddleworth residents whether Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority should use the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan to help decide planning applications. If approved, the plan will become part of the statutory Development Plan.
english_fact_card.when: Referendum on Thursday 10 December 2026.
english_fact_card.who_affected: Residents of the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Area who are registered to vote in local government elections.
english_fact_card.why_now: The referendum date has been set, giving residents the opportunity to influence future planning decisions.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Residents can directly influence local planning policy by voting.
english_fact_card.reader_action: Ensure you are registered to vote and participate in the referendum on 10 December.

If there is only one candidate nominated, then that candidate would be elected without contest. If more than one valid nomination is received, residents will go to the polls on Thursday 3 December 2026 to elect thei This is an opportunity for local people from all backgrounds to represent the interests of their community, raise issues that matter to residents and play a direct role in shaping the future of Royton North and the wider borough. Councillors represent the Council to the community Anyone wishing to stand for election can obtain a nomination pack from the Elections Office at the J.R.Clynes Building, Cultural Quarter, Greaves Street, Oldham, OL1 1AL, between 9am and 5pm, or they can be emailed on request by emailing election@oldham.gov.uk Completed nomination papers must be submitted in person and cannot be accepted by email, post, fax or any other electronic method. Papers can be delivered to the J.R.Clynes Building between 10am and 4pm and no later than 4pm on Friday 6 November

candidates.lead: Primary schools have been recognised for outstanding performance in the 2026 Summer Reading Challenge Read to the Beat
candidates.evidence_text: Primary schools have been recognised for outstanding performance in the 2026 Summer Reading Challenge Read to the Beat The challenge, delivered by The Reading Agency in partnership with public libraries, encouraged children to discover the joy of reading through the theme Read to the Beat, celebrating music, rhythm and the power of stories Royton Hall Primary School, St Martin’s Primary School and Greenfield Primary School were recognised as the schools with the highest participation out of 92 schools taking part across Oldham Representatives from Oldham Libraries and partner Kajima, which supports opportunities to encourage children to read and celebrate their success, visited each school to award book tokens in recognition of pupils’ commitment to reading Kajima have sponsored the Summer Reading Challenge for the sixth year running, encouraging Oldham children towards a lifelong love of books The challenge highlights the importance of partnerships between schools, libraries and local organisations in supporting children’s literacy, building reading confidence and making reading an exciting and rewarding experience

candidates.evidence_text: More than 100,000 visitors flocked to Bolton town centre for this year’s Put Big Light On Festival, making the four-day event one of the borough’s most successful cultural celebrations to date From Thursday 19 to Sunday 22 November, residents and visitors enjoyed an unforgettable programme of illuminated art installations, interactive experiences, street theatre, live performances, and larger-than-life creations across the town centre At the heart of the festival was the stunning Loom of Light installation in Victoria Square, inspired by Bolton’s rich textile heritage, while thousands of visitors explored a diverse programme featuring internationally acclaimed artworks including Helios, DUNDU, Event Horizon, K The festival, delivered by Bolton Council in partnership with Things That Go On Things, also provided a significant boost to local businesses, with visitors spending time in the town’s shops, cafes, restaurants, and cultural venues throughout the event Bolton Council’s Executive Cabinet Member for Culture, Cllr Debbie Newall, said To welcome more than 100,000 visitors to our town centre is a fantastic achievement and a huge boost for our local businesses

evidence_packet.evidence_text: More than 100,000 visitors flocked to Bolton town centre for this year’s Put Big Light On Festival, making the four-day event one of the borough’s most successful cultural celebrations to date From Thursday 19 to Sunday 22 November, residents and visitors enjoyed an unforgettable programme of illuminated art installations, interactive experiences, street theatre, live performances, and larger-than-life creations across the town centre At the heart of the festival was the stunning Loom of Light installation in Victoria Square, inspired by Bolton’s rich textile heritage, while thousands of visitors explored a diverse programme featuring internationally acclaimed artworks including Helios, DUNDU, Event Horizon, K The festival, delivered by Bolton Council in partnership with Things That Go On Things, also provided a significant boost to local businesses, with visitors spending time in the town’s shops, cafes, restaurants, and cultural venues throughout the event Bolton Council’s Executive Cabinet Member for Culture, Cllr Debbie Newall, said To welcome more than 100,000 visitors to our town centre is a fantastic achievement and a huge boost for our local businesses

candidates.lead: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović .
candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . candidates.evidence_text: Nights you don't want to miss - Opening NightCome and join us for our first performance.Buy tickets Seen by over 12 million people across five continents and honoured with more than 85 awards worldwide, Billy Elliot the Musical is one of the most successful and beloved British musicals of all time. Ten years after it last played to audiences in its original home of London and the UK, this landmark production returns at last. Wor Billy! What a sensation, what an inspiration. Billy is a slice of British life that speaks to everyone Set in a northern town during the miners’ strike of 1984/85, the show follows Billy’s journey from the boxing ring to the ballet class, where he discovers a passion for dance that will change his life forever. As Billy dares to dream, his courage unites his family, inspires his community, and proves the transformative power of art. Brought to life by the award-winning creative team behind the film, with iconic music by Elton John, Billy Elliot the Musical is an extraordinary theatrical experience that has captivated audiences around the world. This is the musical that took the nation by surprise and went on to conquer the world. Praised as “Breathtaking. A dazzling 40-carat gem of a show” (Daily Mail), “Dazzling. A triumph” (Independent on Sunday) and “Pure magic” (Sunday Express), Billy Elliot the Musical returns as exhilarating, hilarious and unforgettable as ever; a defining British production finally coming home. A dazzling 40-carat gem of a show Billy boy, this is the greatest musical yet Truly electrifying – this heart-stopping show is a must-see Buy direct from venues with ATG Tickets. Transparent booking fees, no late stage surprises. Palace Theatre Manchester The Palace Theatre of Varieties opened on Whit Monday 1891 and cost its owners the then colossal sum of £40,500. In the late 1970’s the Palace Theatre underwent a major refurbishment and re-opened in 1981 with Andrew Lloyd Webber’s Jesus Christ Superstar and has since then retained its position as the premier provincial touring venue

candidates.lead: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre […] The post Sona Jobarteh Tour appeared first on Band on the Wall
candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. Born in London into a Gambian griot lineage of seven centuries, she began learning the kora at age three with her brother Tunde Jegede and father Sanjally Jobarteh; her cousin was the late Toumani Diabaté. She studied at the Royal College of Music, the Purcell School of Music and SOAS University of London. In 2015 she founded The Gambia Academy, which puts African history and culture at the centre of its curriculum, and she has keynoted forums hosted by the UN and the World Trade Organization. In 2023 Berklee College of Music awarded her an honorary Doctorate in Music alongside Usher and Roberta Flack

candidates.lead: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians.
candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

candidates.evidence_text: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! Across this 5 day course, we’ll be exploring music for film, and working on composing music for the silent film ‘A Trip to the Moon’. The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument. evidence_packet.evidence_text: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! Across this 5 day course, we’ll be exploring music for film, and working on composing music for the silent film ‘A Trip to the Moon’. The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument. Please email learning@bandonthewall.org if you have any questions about this course

The site on King Street has been transformed by the Loungers design team into a warm, eclectic ‘home from home’ – their signature style. Fosforo Lounge’s all‑day menu will cater for every taste, from hearty comfort food to healthier choices and indulgent treats. Families are a major focus, with games, books, colouring materials, high chairs and baby‑changing facilities available for Little Loungers.. . With community at its heart, Fosforo Lounge will offer a welcoming space for regular meet‑ups, business catch‑ups, book clubs, knitting groups, parent‑and‑baby sessions, creative workshops and more. candidates.evidence_text: Clint Boon spinning records on Greek Street on a Saturday afternoon, and it won’t cost you a penny. Stopford Park is throwing a free party to launch Bosden, the first of its new apartment buildings, just up from the Town Hall Clint Boon needs very little introduction round these parts. The Inspiral Carpets man was right in the middle of Madchester and he’s still at it, touring and recently publishing his book, The Manchester Chronicles . He’ll be sharing the decks with DJ, presenter and podcaster Matt There’ll be a talk from John Barratt, co-founder of the Stockport Music Story with his wife Rosemary. John founded the record label Facsimile Liaisons which took him to Strawberry Studios, he’s worked with Easterhouse and Syncopation, and also signed The Family Foundation, Ultrac There will be a pop-up from I Knead Pizza, and it’s also the first chance to have a nosey round the show apartment at Bosden with the remaining apartments going on the market the same day. If you’re tempted to have a look round you can register your interest here Make a weekend of it: Foodie Friday is on across the Market Place and Great Underbank the night before, from 6pm

candidates.evidence_text: Stay connected. Know what's next. We're launching The Inside Track , a new monthly online session designed to help Manchester Digital members stay informed, discover new opportunities and make the most of their membership Whether you've recently joined Manchester Digital or have been part of our community for years, The Inside Track is your chance to catch up with our team, find out what's happening across the network and explore ways to get more involved Taking place on the last Wednesday of each month, these free, members-only sessions will bring you up to speed on the latest developments, events and opportunities across Manchester Digital, all in just 30 minutes Each session will feature a topical focus, alongside practical updates on upcoming events, programmes, speaking opportunities and ways to raise your business's profile There'll also be time to ask questions, share your priorities and find out how we can help you get more value from your membership Our first edition at midday on 25th November will focus on some of the biggest opportunities coming up across the Manchester Digital community

candidates.evidence_text: Five days. Five themes. One city shaping its digital future. The first Manchester Digital Festival takes place from 8–12 February 2027 with its biggest and boldest programme yet. Manchester Digital has unveiled the programme for Manchester Digital Festival 2027 (MDF27 ) , bringin Taking place from Monday 8 to Friday 12 February 2027 , the festival marks an exciting new chapter for Manchester Digital, building on the success of Digital Skills Festival and expanding its scope to celebrate the full breadth of Greater Manchester's digital and technology secto The launch also comes as Manchester Digital celebrates its 25th anniversary , providing an opportunity to reflect on the people, businesses and innovations that have shaped the region's tech ecosystem, while looking ahead to what comes next With 15 events already announced and more to come, the first wave of the MDF27 programme offers everything from industry conferences and leadership discussions to careers events, founder stories and opportunities to explore emerging technologies Tickets for most events are now available , with further announcements expected in the coming months Under the banner Building our digital tomorrow , MDF27 introduces a new five-day format, with each day dedicated to a different theme reflecting the opportunities and challenges facing Greater Manchester's digital and technology sector

From years spent languishing in post-industrial decline to being crowned one of ‘the coolest neighbourhoods in the world’ in the blink of an eye. What’s the story here? Find out with Jonathan Schofield Tours, with whom you’ll track Ancoats’ changes by strolling its streets, crossing its canals, and taking a look inside one of its most fascinating buildings Starting at Cutting Room Square, your expert tour guide will reveal the layers of history that make Ancoats special, from its place in establishing Manchester’s reputation as ‘Cottonopolis’ to the notorious street gangs, or ‘scuttlers’, who once patrolled and fought here But this winsome stroll is also about the urban regeneration and cultural energy of Ancoats today, which boasts everything from grassroots theatres to Manchester’s only Michelin-starred restaurant

Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

Engels lived here, on and off, for 22 years, during which time Marx would stay with him for long periods. The remarkable tale of two men who changed the political world is told on thi In the 1840s, industrial Manchester appeared to confirm for both Engels and Marx the truth behind their ideas of how society was ordered and where it was inevitably headed. It seemed clear to them how the tensions between the ‘bourgeoisie’ and ‘proletariat’ would ultimately lead It would probably not have been clear to them that present commemorations in Greater Manchester would include a climbing wall in the shape of the face and beard of Engels Still, the fact they filtered their ideas as young men through the experience of Manchester was crucial. In August, Nothing Gold Can Stay took Robert Frost’s poem about transience as its starting point. Where that show dwelt on things passing, this one is more interested in what lasts The four contributing artists each approach time differently, thinking about how the past and the future shape the way ideas are understood. Anna Clough, a Cumbrian-born artist based at Salford’s Paradise Works, has made walking performances tracing mining landscapes from the Neo Sheffield’s Charlotte Dawson treats everyday objects – souvenirs, collections – as vessels for memory. Olivia England, who graduated from Manchester School of Art alongside Clough, reworks found objects, text and imagery through bookbinding and print, while London-based Elliot Fo Seeing the work from a perspective that isn’t your own is meant to open up conversations about the legacy of ideas, collective memory and what our actions leave behind for people we’ll never meet

candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Selection: Selected in football shortlist before writing.

candidates.lead: Cherki calls for more following Napoli draw
candidates.evidence_text: Rasmus Højlund grabbed the opener for the visitors after 55 minutes, latching onto Billy Gilmour’s pass before drilling into the net. Enzo Maresca’s men reacted well to the setback and levelled 12 minutes later thanks to a thunderous left-footed strike from midfield maestro Ayyoub Bouaddi, who claimed his first-ever goal in senior football. With City in the ascendancy, the visitors broke on a quick counter and restored their lead through Noa Lang’s controlled volley. But Maresca’s men showed grit and determination to fight back for a second time, with UEFA’s Player of the Match Cherki precisely finding the net with four minutes of normal time left at the Etihad to earn a point. Despite another sparkling individual performance, the Frenchman made it clear that the three points are always the utmost priority. “I don’t care about scoring my goal today. I want to win, just that,” said Cherki in an honest interview after the game. “Today we played good but we didn’t put a lot of energy I think. “We need to do more. We need to win this game, today I don’t care about scoring my goal, we need to win the game. We try to put all we have on the pitch. Sometimes the game is not like how you want. “Today it’s like the last two or three games. We need to work more and come back for a win. Just that.” The draw means we have three wins, one draw and one defeat in the competition this term, with three fixtures left of the League Phase. Attention now turns to Sunday’s huge Premier League clash away to league-leaders Arsenal and Cherki explained that City only have one intention heading into London. “We are in a difficult position, that is true because we didn’t win the game,” he continued. “We’re going to London to win the game. “Nothing more.”

candidates.evidence_text: Prefer the Guardian on Google 1. Moyes: ‘I want Jack to show more’ David Moyes has said he wants Jack Grealish to produce more for Everton as he prepares to reintegrate the playmaker into the squad Grealish has missed Everton’s past four games mainly for disciplinary reasons having failed to report for training before last month’s Carabao Cup win over Newcastle. His last appearance for the team was in the 2-0 loss to Chelsea on 17 October but he is fit and available for Mon “He has served his punishment and we will treat him as we were treating him before,” the Everton manager said. “We will get on with things. The team is doing really well at the moment and what I don’t want to do is turn it into a Jack story because it shouldn’t be.” The 31-year-old played in a behind-closed-doors fixture against Derby last week andalso apologised on social media for being unable to help the team, who won three of four matches in his absence. Grealish, however, had struggled to replicate last season’s form impact when joining He added: “Jack can offer us a lot. I want more from him, I want him to show more than he has done. I want him to give me more assists, more goals. There’s lots of things about him which we need and he’s good at retaining the ball, giving us good possession, carrying. So we hope The Everton manager has backed Jordan Pickford to respond strongly to the threat from James Trafford to his England place, following after the Leeds goalkeeper’s inclusion and impressive display in the Nations League win over Spain

Moyes: ‘I want Jack to show more’ David Moyes has said he wants Jack Grealish to produce more for Everton as he prepares to reintegrate the playmaker into the squad Grealish has missed Everton’s past four games mainly for disciplinary reasons having failed to report for training before last month’s Carabao Cup win over Newcastle. His last appearance for the team was in the 2-0 loss to Chelsea on 17 October but he is fit and available for Mon “He has served his punishment and we will treat him as we were treating him before,” the Everton manager said. “We will get on with things. The team is doing really well at the moment and what I don’t want to do is turn it into a Jack story because it shouldn’t be.” The 31-year-old played in a behind-closed-doors fixture against Derby last week andalso apologised on social media for being unable to help the team, who won three of four matches in his absence. Grealish, however, had struggled to replicate last season’s form impact when joining He added: “Jack can offer us a lot. I want more from him, I want him to show more than he has done. I want him to give me more assists, more goals. There’s lots of things about him which we need and he’s good at retaining the ball, giving us good possession, carrying. So we hope The Everton manager has backed Jordan Pickford to respond strongly to the threat from James Trafford to his England place, following after the Leeds goalkeeper’s inclusion and impressive display in the Nations League win over Spain
